resources.string: Enter the address of the computer or server that runs smartpower.py to see your power strip.
The server can\'t be reached. Check the address and that smartpower.py is running.
The server rejected the token. Check it in Settings.
The server answered with an error. Try again in a moment.
The server is running, but no power strip has connected to it. Set up the strip so it knows this server\'s address.
Leave empty to use the default name.
The strip has not confirmed the change yet.
For example 192.168.1.20, 203.0.113.5:7896 or https://power.example.com (port 8080 if none is given).
That doesn\'t look like an address. Use an IP or host name, optionally with :port.
Leave empty if the server runs without --token.
Connect a new or reset strip to your Wi-Fi and to this server, right from your phone.
Darwish Smart Power controls MTTL-W01 power strips through your own server. No cloud account is needed.
Hold the strip\'s main button for about 10 seconds until the light blinks fast.
In the phone\'s Wi-Fi settings join the network TONLY_TAP_XXXXXXX. Its password is LGU_ followed by the same 7 characters. If Android says there is no internet, choose to stay connected.
Come back here, fill in the fields below and tap Send.
When it says done, switch the phone back to your home Wi-Fi. The strip appears on the home screen within a minute.
The IPv4 address the strip will connect to: the computer\'s home IP, or the public IP of your VPS.
2.4 GHz networks only. The strip cannot use 5 GHz.
Done. The strip will join your Wi-Fi and connect to %1$s. Switch the phone back to your home Wi-Fi now.
The phone is not connected to any Wi-Fi. Join the strip\'s TONLY_TAP network first.
The strip did not answer. Make sure it is blinking fast (setup mode) and the phone is on its TONLY_TAP network.
The server IP must be an IPv4 address such as 192.168.1.20.
The strip cannot accept a Wi-Fi name that contains \":\".
The strip cannot accept a Wi-Fi password that contains \":\".
